Architecture (drawn network diagrams)

Draw the network path of a service, bind each device element to its SATOM appliance, and read it live by layer (L2, L3, L4, L7). FortiGate interfaces and policies with hit counters are drawn segment to segment, back-ends answer an HTTP probe, and a flow trace asks every FortiGate on the way for its own verdict.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereOperations → Architecture (every ADOM) (URL /net-architecture/)

What is it?#

Architecture is a page where you draw the network path of a service, the Internet, LANs, segments and VLANs, firewalls, WAFs, load balancers and back-end servers, and SATOM lays what the devices report on top of your drawing. You state what the network is. SATOM then reads the bound FortiGates and back-ends to check the drawing against the live devices.

ℹ️Note

New in 3.1.0. The cache-based fleet map that used to be called Architecture is now Operations → Service Diagram (/architecture/); see Service Diagram. The Service Diagram is derived: SATOM draws it from the FortiWeb cache. Architecture is drawn: you place every element yourself.

What does it do?#

  • Drawings: named diagrams stored in SATOM. Every drawing is listed in every ADOM. Pick one from the Drawing list.
  • Elements: Internet, LAN, Segment / VLAN, FortiGate, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer, Back-end server, Management host and Other host. Device elements can be bound to a SATOM appliance of the same kind.
  • Read devices: reads the bound devices now, read-only and in parallel, and draws the result as a live overlay. You can repeat the read every 30 s.
  • Layers L2, L3, L4 and L7 each show a different part of that overlay (see Layers).
  • Trace a flow: enter source, destination, protocol and port. Each FortiGate on the drawn path answers with its own route and policy lookup, and the path is drawn in colour.
  • Autosave with Undo / Redo, and versioned saves so two people can edit one drawing without overwriting each other.
  • After Read devices, a bound device element offers Device (the appliance page), Path Diagnostics (with that appliance already selected) and Sentinel in the inspector.

The canvas uses the same dark network-design style as the Service Diagram. Policy flows are animated, and hovering an element lights up everything connected to it. The legend in the lower-left corner explains the current layer.

Requirements#

  • At least one drawing. A user with configuration write permission creates it (see Create a drawing).
  • For the live overlay, appliances registered in SATOM (see Appliances):
  • FortiGate elements are read over the FortiGate REST API, with the credentials SATOM already holds for the appliance.
  • FortiWeb elements show their server policies from SATOM's device cache, so the FortiWeb must have been synchronised at least once.
  • Back-end server, Management host and Other host elements are probed only when you give them a Probe URL.
  • FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer elements can be bound and linked, but nothing is read from them live.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Opening the page, Read devices, the layers and Trace a flow need the legacy view gate. Any read permission grants it (for example monitoring.view), and all system profiles have it.

Creating, editing and deleting drawings need the legacy config_write gate, for example operations.apply or appliances.apply. Without it:

  • New drawing, Undo, Redo, Elements, Link, the delete button and Delete drawing are hidden.
  • The inspector shows the element's values read-only, and elements cannot be dragged.
  • The save, create and delete endpoints answer 403.

The Path Diagnostics and Sentinel links on a device element appear only when your profile can open those pages.

❗Important

What SATOM reads depends on the ADOM you are in. The palette and the SATOM appliance list show only the appliances the current ADOM can see. In the FortiGate ADOM that means only FortiGates. An element bound to a device of another ADOM is drawn but not read or linked (its status dot is grey). Open the drawing in the Global ADOM to read every product at once.

How to use#

Create a drawing#

  1. Open Operations → Architecture.
  2. Type a name in New drawing name and click New drawing. Names are unique and up to 120 characters long.
  3. The new, empty drawing opens. Pick other drawings from the Drawing list.

Add and link elements#

  1. Click Elements. The palette lists every appliance the current ADOM can see, grouped by product, with a search box (Search the fleet…). Under Generic it lists every element type.
  2. Click an appliance to add it already bound to that appliance, with its address as IP address. An appliance that is already on the drawing shows ✓ drawn, and clicking it selects the existing element instead.
  3. Click a generic type to add an unbound element, for example Segment / VLAN or Back-end server.
  4. Drag elements into place. Drag the empty canvas to pan, and use the mouse wheel or the zoom buttons to zoom. The fit button frames the whole drawing.
  5. Click Link, then click two elements to connect them. Click Link again to leave link mode.
  6. Select an element and fill in the inspector on the right (see Configuration).
  7. To remove an element, select it and click the delete button or press Delete. Its links go with it.

Every change saves itself after about a second. The badge at the top right reads Unsaved…, Saving… and then Saved with the time.

Put firewall policies on the drawing#

A policy can only be drawn between networks that SATOM can tie to the FortiGate's interfaces.

  1. Add a FortiGate element and bind it to its appliance (SATOM appliance).
  2. For each LAN, Segment / VLAN or Internet element behind that firewall, set Behind FortiGate to the FortiGate element.
  3. Either enter the FortiGate interface (for example port2), or enter the network's Network (CIDR). Without an interface name, SATOM matches the network to the FortiGate port whose address falls inside that CIDR.
  4. Click Read devices.

Each policy is then drawn as an arrow from its source network to its destination network (green for accept, red for deny). Select the FortiGate and click a policy in the inspector to highlight its path. Click it again to clear the highlight.

Read the devices#

  1. Click Read devices. The status line reports how many devices, probes and policy flows were read, and at what time.
  2. Tick every 30 s to repeat the read while the tab is visible.
  3. Select an element to see its live detail in the inspector.

Status dots on the elements: green means read, amber means some reads failed but policies were read, red means the read or probe failed, and grey means the element is bound to a device this ADOM cannot see.

Trace a flow#

  1. Click Trace a flow. You can also select an element that has an IP address and click Trace from here or Trace to here.
  2. Enter Source IP and Destination IP, choose TCP, UDP or ICMP, and for TCP or UDP enter the destination Port (default 443).
  3. Click Trace.

The path is drawn from the source to the destination: cyan if allowed, red if denied and amber if the verdict is unknown. The inspector shows the verdict with its reason and lists every firewall asked, with its ingress → egress interface, gateway, route, matched policy and action. A firewall that could not be read is listed with its error and is never skipped silently.

When a TCP trace passes a FortiWeb or FortiADC, the inspector offers Validate with Path Diagnostics. That button opens Path Diagnostics with the appliance, destination hostname, port and scheme filled in.

Click Clear or press Esc to remove the trace.

Work as a team#

Open pages check for a colleague's save every 15 seconds and redraw. The badge then reads Updated by with the colleague's name and the time. If you change the drawing while someone else saves it, their version is shown, the badge reads Updated by … — your change is in Undo, and Undo brings your version back.

Undo and redo: the buttons, Ctrl+Z, and Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y).

Delete a drawing#

Click Delete drawing below the canvas and confirm. The drawing is removed for everyone.

Layers#

The layer buttons change what the overlay shows. L3 is the default.

Layer On the links On the elements In the FortiGate inspector
L2 Port, MAC, speed and VLAN; green when the link is up, red dashed when it is down Networks: VLAN tag (or untagged) and interface. Hosts: the MAC address a FortiGate learned for their IP (ARP), and the port it was seen on Ports (MAC, link, speed, errors) and the ARP table
L3 Port and its address Addresses and networks Routes, and policies with source → destination addresses, hits, bytes and last use
L4 Port RX / TX byte counters Probe answer and latency Policies with services, hits and active sessions
L7 FortiWeb server policies drawn to the back-ends they publish (policy → :port) Probe status code and latency; on a FortiWeb, the number of server policies Policies as in L3, without routes. The FortiWeb inspector lists server policies, published VIPs and ports, pool and back-ends

In L3 the policy arrows are labelled #<id> <name>. In L4 they show the services, active sessions and hit count. The implicit-deny counter (traffic that no policy matched) is shown under the policy table.

An L7 arrow is drawn only when an element on the drawing has the back-end's exact IP address. In the FortiWeb inspector a back-end marked ✓ is on the drawing.

Configuration#

Inspector fields per element:

Field Applies to Description Example
Label All Name shown on the element (80 characters) Web DMZ
Network (CIDR) Internet, LAN, Segment / VLAN The network. Must be a valid network 192.0.2.0/24
VLAN tag Internet, LAN, Segment / VLAN Shown in L2 and L3 120
Behind FortiGate Internet, LAN, Segment / VLAN The FortiGate element this network sits behind fgt-01
FortiGate interface Internet, LAN, Segment / VLAN The port it hangs off. Optional when the CIDR identifies it port2
IP address All other types The host's address. Used by the trace and by ARP and L7 matching 192.0.2.20
SATOM appliance FortiGate, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer Binds the element to an appliance of the same kind fweb-01 (192.0.2.5)
Probe URL Back-end server, Management host, Other host One HTTP GET per read. Must start with http:// or https:// https://192.0.2.20/health
Show response header Back-end server, Management host, Other host One response header to display Server
Note All Free text, shown as the tooltip (400 characters) Primary web pool

Example#

🧪Example — Is HTTPS from the LAN to the web server allowed?

A drawing has an Internet element, a FortiGate element bound to fgt-01, a LAN 198.51.100.0/24 and a Segment / VLAN 192.0.2.0/24 (both Behind FortiGate = fgt-01), and a Back-end server 192.0.2.20 linked to the segment, with Probe URL https://192.0.2.20/.

  1. Click Read devices. In L3, the arrow #12 LAN-to-DMZ runs from the LAN to the segment. In L4 the same arrow reads #12 HTTPS · 3 sess · 4812 hits.
  2. Select the back-end and click Trace to here. Enter 198.51.100.50 as Source IP, keep TCP / 443, and click Trace.
  3. The path turns cyan. The inspector lists fgt-01 port1 → port2, policy #12 LAN-to-DMZ · accept.

Result#

  • Every save stores the whole drawing and writes an audit entry netarch.save (with the number of elements and links). Creating and deleting a drawing write netarch.create and netarch.delete. See Audit log.
  • Every trace writes netarch.trace with source, destination, protocol, port and verdict.
  • Read devices and the trace change nothing on any device and store nothing. Every value is read when you ask for it and is not cached.

Troubleshooting#

"A drawing needs a name." / "A drawing called … already exists."#

Enter a name, or pick a name that no other drawing uses.

The badge reads "Not saved: …"#

Possible causes: the drawing has an error. A drawing with any error is refused whole and nothing is stored. Common messages:

  • element <id>: '<value>' is not a network: fix Network (CIDR).
  • element <id>: '<value>' is not an IP address: fix IP address.
  • element <id>: probe URL must start with http:// or https://
  • element <id>: gateway must be a FortiGate element
  • element <id>: appliance <n> is not visible here: you bound a device that the current ADOM cannot see. Bind it from the Global ADOM or from the device's own ADOM.
  • element <id>: <name> is a <kind>, not a <kind>: the appliance is a different product from the element type.
  • too many elements (…, max 300) / too many links (…, max 600)

Solution: correct the field named in the message, or press Undo. Verification: the badge reads Saved with the time.

"Updated by … — your change is in Undo"#

A colleague saved the drawing after your page loaded. Their version is on screen. Press Undo to bring yours back. It then saves on top of theirs.

A policy says "not drawn: portN"#

The policy uses an interface with no network element behind it. Add a network element with Behind FortiGate set to that firewall and FortiGate interface = portN (or a CIDR that contains the port's address).

No policy arrows appear#

  • Read devices has not run yet. The legend ends with Press Read devices.
  • The FortiGate element is not bound, or is bound in an ADOM that cannot see it (grey dot).
  • No network element has Behind FortiGate set to that firewall.

The FortiGate shows errors in the inspector#

Each read is reported on its own, in the form <API path>: <error>. A failed read leaves the other tables standing. Check that the appliance's API credentials are valid and that its admin profile can read interfaces, routes, ARP and firewall policies. See FortiGate.

"Live read failed: HTTP …"#

The overlay request itself failed. Reload the page and check your session.

The trace verdict is unknown#

The reason is shown next to the verdict:

  • no drawn FortiGate sits between these addresses: draw the firewall and link it, or set Behind FortiGate on the networks.
  • no FortiGate on the way could be read: see the hop errors, for example not bound to a readable FortiGate or no route to <ip>.
  • more than 6 firewalls: stopped: the trace asks at most six firewalls.

The source is not on the drawing (or destination) means that no element has that IP address and no drawn network contains it. A public address with no network drawn for it is placed on the Internet element, when the drawing has one without a CIDR.

"a tcp/udp trace needs a destination port 1-65535"#

Enter a port, or choose ICMP.

A back-end probe shows "no answer"#

The probe gets no HTTP answer within about 4 seconds. The error is shown in the inspector. The probe runs from the SATOM server, so check that SATOM can reach that address.

Advanced#

Advanced How the trace decides
  • For each FortiGate, SATOM asks the device for its route to the source (the ingress interface) and to the destination (the egress interface). It then asks the device's own policy lookup for that ingress interface, addresses, protocol and port. SATOM never evaluates a rule base itself.
  • The walk continues to the network drawn behind the egress interface and stops on the first deny, at the destination network, or when no firewall is drawn beyond. A firewall whose ingress and egress are the same interface is not on the path and is skipped.
  • A deny with no matching policy is reported as implicit deny: no policy matches.
Advanced What is read, and from where
  • FortiGate (live, REST, read-only): interfaces and their monitor counters, ARP table, IPv4 routing table, firewall policies with hit count, bytes, packets, last use and active sessions, and the implicit-deny counter. Each request times out after 8 seconds, and up to eight reads run in parallel.
  • FortiWeb (device cache, never live): up to 200 server policies, with VIPs, service ports, pool, back-ends and web protection profile. These are the same helpers the Service Diagram uses, so the two pages agree.
  • Probes: one GET to the URL stored in the element, without certificate verification and without following redirects. A 3xx or 4xx counts as an answer, and only 5xx or no response counts as a failure. The overlay request carries no address, so the probe goes only to URLs saved in the drawing.
  • Switches are not read. Draw the segments they carry.
Advanced Storage and limits
  • Drawings live in the arch_diagrams table: name, the drawing as JSON (elements and links only) and who last saved it. Live data is never stored.
  • Each save sends the version it was based on. A stale version gets 409 with the stored drawing.
  • Limits: 300 elements, 600 links, one link per pair of elements, and no element linked to itself.
